# DataTable

Display and categorise a lot of data with rows and columns.
See [DataTable guidelines<i className="ds-icon-launch"></i>](https://design-system.airbus.corp/components/data-table/design/)

### Introduction

The `DataTable` component includes sorting, column resizing, row virtualization, etc.

For a basic and static HTML table, use the <LinkTo kind="Components/Table" story="docs">Table</LinkTo> component.

**Memoization** : DataTable uses [@tanstack/react-table](https://tanstack.com/table/latest) internally, and it relies on memoization to determine when state and side effects should update,
So you should memoize `data` and `columns` which you pass to the DataTable component.

**Layout** : Navigate to the Templates category to understand <LinkTo kind="General/Templates/DataTable" story="fixed-layout">how to setup a responsive layout</LinkTo>

### Sort

Use the `sortBy` prop to define the initial sort order.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Sortby} />

Use the `maxSortColCount` prop to limit the number of columns that can be sorted at the same time.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.MaxSort} />

### Pagination

Pagination is automatically displayed if `data` length exceeds `defaultRowsPerPage`.

It can be disabled using `disablePagination` prop. In this case pagination can be displayed and managed externally.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Pagination} />

Rows per page feature is optional. When enabled, pagination will always be displayed, independently of `data` length.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.RowsPerPage} />

### Custom pagination

Pagination has certain props that are mandatory and they are passed internally.
You can pass the optional props that suits your needs. This is an example to enable `goto` and customize `Rows Per Page`.


<Canvas of={DataTableStories.CustomPagination} />

### Resize

Set `allowResize` to true to enable column resizing.<br />
You may disable resize by columns using the `disableResizing` parameter, like the creation column in this example.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Resize} />

### Cells

You can customize cells and headers by using `cell` and `header` parameters.<br />
Typings are available for the corresponding parameters : `DataTableCellContext` and `DataTableHeaderContext`.<br />
These types are re-exported from @tanstack/react-table : https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/api/core/column-def

```js
// display a '%' sign after the value
cell: ({ getValue }) => `${getValue()}%`;
// display a '-' sign if the getValue function returns empty
cell: ({ getValue }) => (getValue() ? getValue() : "-");
// custom cell component
cell: MyCustomCell;
// custom header component
header: MyCustomHeader;
```

By using the `accessor` and `cell` parameters together, you can parse and format data separately.

```js
{
  header: "Creation",
  accessorFn: (row) => new Date(row.creation),
  cell: ({ getValue }) => getValue().toLocaleDateString(),
  sortingFn: "datetime",
}
```

Here is an example with custom cells and headers including `Link`, `Chip`, `Input` and `Menu` components.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Cells} />

### Default Selection

Use `defaultSelectedRows` to define initial selected rows.<br />
Optionally you can use `getRowId` to derive a unique id for any given row instead of using indexes.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.DefaultSelection} />

### Expandable

Expandable tables allow user to evaluate additional information without losing their context.
This feature is **incompatible with virtualization**.

Height of the expanded content can be defined using `height` or `getRowHeight` options.

Recommendations

- Indent the content of expanded row to align with the first column
- Use row dividers to help understand boundaries (using `allowDividers` prop)

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Expandable} />

```css
.datatable-expandedrow-example {
  padding-left: 2.5rem;
  line-height: 1.25rem;
}
```

### Virtualized

When rendering a very large amount of data, you may observe performance issues.<br />
Set `allowVirtualization` to true to enable virtualization. The downside is you have to set a fixed `height`.<br />
Virtualization ensure a limited amount of HTML Elements are reused in the DOM, providing huge performance improvements.<br />
The example below loads 10 000 rows of data in the table.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Virtualized} />

### Persistence

User preferences or client side DataTable manipulations like column sorting or resizing will often benefit from being persisted.
We offer a simple mechanism to allow that via the `onStateUpdate` callback.

In this example we use <a href="https://github.com/astoilkov/use-local-storage-state">use-local-storage-state</a>
library to persist the state in localStorage.<br />
If you change the column sizes or sorts and reload the page you will see that the states are persisted.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Persistence} />

### Controlled

This sample show how to control the data displayed in the DataTable externally via the `onQueryUpdate` callback.<br />
This callback gets called each time an interaction requires reloading of the data (pagination, sort, etc.).<br />
In addition to the `onQueryUpdate` callback you will have to handle those props : `loading`, `pageCount`, `rowCount`.

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Controlled} />

### Filtering & controlled pagination

This example show an approach on building filters on top of the `DataTable` component.<br />
In this case, the component won't reset pagination automatically when reloading the data.

To control the pagination
- use `paginationProps.page` and `paginationProps.onPageChange` to manage the current page index
- use `disablePagination` to disable the internal pagination and display it externally

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.ControlledPagination} />

### Infinite

This sample show how to use the `DataTable` as an infinite table,
by querying more rows each time you click on the "Load More" button.

For this to work you need to set `disablePagination=true` and `allowVirtualization=true` (for optimisation purpose)

<Canvas of={DataTableStories.Infinite} />
